catCompanionRules: A cat Companion is explicitly a non-player travel companion, never the player's Portrait.
Keep it small, secondary, outside the portrait composition slot, and without distinctive identity-design emphasis.
Do not infer, imitate, or pre-empt the player's real cat identity before user photos arrive.
Do not export a standalone cat, pose set, identity board, or reusable Portrait from a companion scene.
Do not use the orange-white cat from style references or any invented cat as a substitute for the player cat.
allCompanionRules: Use only the explicitly listed species and count for each rare variant.
Keep companions subtle and visually secondary to both landmark and future player Portrait.
Companions must not overlap safeBounds or obscure landmark recognition points.

globalConstraints: Every ordinary variant contains no cat, animal, person, date, postmark, caption, logo, watermark, readable sign, pseudo-text, UI, slot frame, or anchor mark.
A rare variant contains only its explicitly authorized Companion and no player cat or substitute Portrait.
Use reliable real photographs or authoritative visual sources for landmark silhouette and layout, and record provenance and rights notes.
Keep the landmark immediately recognizable and preserve defining proportions and structural relationships.
Reserve an unobstructed, low-detail, low-contrast portrait slot away from landmark recognition points and future copy and postmark zones.

Use locked B intensity: thin warm gray-brown linework, low-saturation sage green, ochre, faded vermilion, generous negative space, subtle warm-white paper texture, restrained watercolor bleed, and quiet nostalgia.
Avoid photorealism, 3D, flat vector art, neon, high saturation, hard digital gradients, thick black outlines, crowded backgrounds, malformed architecture or anatomy, and copied source-photo pixels.
